[text-22] list item "README"
[text-23] heading "Code of conduct"
[text-24] heading "Contributing"
[text-25] list item "Apache-2.0 license"
[text-26] list item "Security"
[text-27] table row "Documentation | API reference"
[text-28] "Playwright is a framework for web automation and testing. It drives Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with a single API — in your tests, in your scripts, and as a tool for AI agents."
[text-29] heading "Get Started"
[text-30] "Choose the path that fits your workflow:"
[text-31] table row " | Best for | Install"
[text-32] table row "Playwright Test | End-to-end testing | npm init playwright@latest"
[text-33] table row "Playwright CLI | Coding agents (Claude Code, Copilot) | npm i -g @playwright/cli@latest"
[text-34] table row "Playwright MCP | AI agents and LLM-driven automation | npx @playwright/mcp@latest"
[text-35] table row "Playwright Library | Browser automation scripts | npm i playwright"
[text-36] table row "VS Code Extension | Test authoring and debugging in VS Code | Install from Marketplace"
[text-37] heading "Playwright Test"
[text-38] "Playwright Test is a full-featured test runner built for end-to-end testing. It runs tests across Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit with full browser isolation, auto-waiting, and web-first assertions."
[text-39] heading "Install"
[text-40] code "npm init playwright@latest"
[text-41] "Or add manually:"
[text-42] code "npm i -D @playwright/test\nnpx playwright install"
[text-43] heading "Write a test"
[text-44] code "import { test, expect } from '@playwright/test';\n\ntest('has title', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\n  await expect(page).toHaveTitle(/Playwright/);\n});\n\ntest('get started link', async ({ page }) => {\n  await page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');\n  await page.getBy"
[text-45] heading "Run tests"
[text-46] code "npx playwright test"
[text-47] "Tests run in parallel across all configured browsers, in headless mode by default. Each test gets a fresh browser context — full isolation with near-zero overhead."
[text-48] heading "Key capabilities"
[text-49] "Auto-wait and web-first assertions. No artificial timeouts. Playwright waits for elements to be actionable, and assertions automatically retry until conditions are met."
[text-50] "Locators. Find elements with resilient locators that mirror how users see the page:"
[text-51] code "page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' })\npage.getByLabel('Email')\npage.getByPlaceholder('Search...')\npage.getByTestId('login-form')"
[text-52] "Test isolation. Each test runs in its own browser context — equivalent to a fresh browser profile. Save authentication state once and reuse it across tests:"
[text-53] code "// Save state after login\nawait page.context().storageState({ path: 'auth.json' });\n\n// Reuse in other tests\ntest.use({ storageState: 'auth.json' });"
[text-54] "Tracing. Capture execution traces, screenshots, and videos on failure. Inspect every action, DOM snapshot, network request, and console message in the Trace Viewer:"
[text-55] code "// playwright.config.ts\nexport default defineConfig({\n  use: {\n    trace: 'on-first-retry',\n  },\n});"
[text-56] code "npx playwright show-trace trace.zip"
[text-57] "Parallelism. Tests run in parallel by default across all configured browsers."
[text-58] "Full testing documentation"
[text-59] heading "Playwright CLI"
[text-60] "Playwright CLI is a command-line interface for browser automation designed for coding agents. It's more token-efficient than MCP — commands avoid loading large tool schemas and accessibility trees into the model context."
[text-61] code "npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest"
[text-62] "Optionally install skills for richer agent integration:"
[text-63] code "playwright-cli install --skills"
[text-64] heading "Usage"
[text-65] "Point your coding agent at a task:"
[text-66] code "Test the \"add todo\" flow on https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc using playwright-cli.\nTake screenshots for all successful and failing scenarios."
[text-67] "Or run commands directly:"
[text-68] code "playwright-cli open https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc/ --headed"
[text-69] "playwright-cli type \"Buy groceries\""
[text-70] "playwright-cli press Enter"
[text-71] "playwright-cli screenshot"
[text-72] heading "Session monitoring"
[text-73] "Use playwright-cli show to open a visual dashboard with live screencast previews of all running browser sessions. Click any session to zoom in and take remote control."
[text-74] code "playwright-cli show"
[text-75] table row "Full CLI documentation | GitHub"
[text-76] heading "Playwright MCP"
[text-77] "The Playwright MCP server gives AI agents full browser control through the Model Context Protocol. Agents interact with pages using structured accessibility snapshots — no vision models or screenshots required."
[text-78] heading "Setup"
[text-79] "Add to your MCP client (VS Code, Cursor, Claude Desktop, Windsurf, etc.):"
[text-80] "{"
[text-81] "  \"mcpServers\": {"
[text-82] "    \"playwright\": {"
[text-83] "      \"command\": \"npx\","
[text-84] "      \"args\": [\"@playwright/mcp@latest\"]"
[text-85] "    }"
[text-86] "  }"
[text-87] "}"
[text-88] "One-click install for VS Code:"
[text-89] "For Claude Code:"
[text-90] code "claude mcp add playwright npx @playwright/mcp@latest"
[text-91] heading "How it works"
[text-92] "Ask your AI assistant to interact with any web page:"
[text-93] code "Navigate to https://demo.playwright.dev/todomvc and add a few todo items."
[text-94] "The agent sees the page as a structured accessibility tree:"
[text-95] code "- heading \"todos\" [level=1]"
[text-96] "- textbox \"What needs to be done?\" [ref=e5]"
[text-97] "- listitem:"
[text-98] "  - checkbox \"Toggle Todo\" [ref=e10]"
[text-99] "  - text: \"Buy groceries\""
[text-100] "It uses element refs like e5 and e10 to click, type, and interact — deterministically and without visual ambiguity. Tools cover navigation, form filling, screenshots, network mocking, storage management, and more."
[text-101] table row "Full MCP documentation | GitHub"
[text-102] heading "Playwright Library"
[text-103] "Use playwright as a library for browser automation scripts — web scraping, PDF generation, screenshot capture, and any workflow that needs programmatic browser control without a test runner."
[text-104] code "npm i playwright"
[text-105] heading "Examples"
[text-106] "Take a screenshot:"
[text-107] code "import { chromium } from 'playwright';"
[text-108] "const browser = await chromium.launch();"
[text-109] "const page = await browser.newPage();"
[text-110] "await page.goto('https://playwright.dev/');"
[text-111] "await page.screenshot({ path: 'screenshot.png' });"
[text-112] "await browser.close();"
[text-113] "Generate a PDF:"
[text-114] "await page.pdf({ path: 'page.pdf', format: 'A4' });"
[text-115] "Emulate a mobile device:"
[text-116] code "import { chromium, devices } from 'playwright';"
[text-117] "const context = await browser.newContext(devices['iPhone 15']);"
[text-118] "const page = await context.newPage();"
[text-119] "await page.screenshot({ path: 'mobile.png' });"
[text-120] "Intercept network requests:"
[text-121] "await page.route('**/*.{png,jpg,jpeg}', route => route.abort());"
[text-122] table row "Library documentation | API reference"
[text-123] heading "VS Code Extension"
[text-124] "The Playwright VS Code extension brings test running, debugging, and code generation directly into your editor."
[text-125] "Run and debug tests from the editor with a single click. Set breakpoints, inspect variables, and step through test execution with a live browser view."
[text-126] "Generate tests with CodeGen. Click \"Record new\" to open a browser — navigate and interact with your app while Playwright writes the test code for you."
[text-127] "Pick locators. Hover over any element in the browser to see the best available locator, then click to copy it to your clipboard."
[text-128] "Trace Viewer integration. Enable \"Show Trace Viewer\" in the sidebar to get a full execution trace after each test run — DOM snapshots, network requests, console logs, and screenshots at every step."
[text-129] table row "Install the extension | VS Code guide"
[text-130] heading "Cross-Browser Support"
[text-131] table row " | Linux | macOS | Windows"
[text-132] table row "Chromium1 157.0.8103.6 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅"
[text-133] table row "WebKit 27.2 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅"
[text-134] table row "Firefox 158.0 | ✅ | ✅ | ✅"
[text-135] "Headless and headed execution on all platforms. 1 Uses Chrome for Testing by default."
[text-136] heading "Other Languages"
[text-137] "Playwright is also available for Python, .NET, and Java."

options.scroll_down: scroll the page down a screen, when no block further down holds what the words ask for
options.back: go back to the previous page
options.press: press a key: enter, escape, space or an arrow key
options.read: read the page aloud or show its contents
options.clear: clear the text in the focused field
options.stop: stop what the browser is doing
options.none: not a command for this page: a remark, a question, a name, noise
options.play: music: find a song or video by the words and play it now, on YouTube or on this site as the words point — never the page's play button, which is a click
options.play_next: music: find a song by the words and play it after the one playing
options.queue: music: find a song by the words and add it to the end of the queue
options.say_time: appliance: say the time and date — 15:27, Thursday 22 October
options.say_weather: appliance: say today's weather in London, the home city — words naming another place or a website are a search, not this — London: 13°C, partly cloudy now; today high 15°C, low 8°C, rain 20%; coming hours 14:00 14°C, 15:00 15°C, 16:00 15°C, 17:00 14°C, 18:00 13°C, 19:00 12°C; coming days 2026-10-24 14°C/9°C Rain, rain 70%, 2026-10-25 13°C/7°C Overcast, rain 30%, 2026-10-26 15°C/8°C Clear sky, rain 5%
options.say_playing: appliance: say the song playing — nothing playing
options.say_timer: appliance: say how long is left on the timer — no timer set

slot.instructions: Which words of the transcript are the thing the command carries verbatim: the address to open, the search terms, the song to play, the text to type, the key to press? Never the command word itself: "play X" carries X. Choose none when it carries none.

options.none: the command carries no words of its own

extent.instructions: Only when the action scrolls the page or a scrolling part of it: how far? Choose words when the words give a number of screens or pages; screen when they say nothing of how far. Ignored for every other action.

options.words: as many screens as the number the words carry
options.little: a little: a third of a screen
options.screen: one screen, as Page Down does
options.end: all the way: to the bottom, or to the top going up

where.instructions: Where do the words point: at something on this page, at something on github.com that is not on this page, or somewhere else on the web?

options.page: on this page: one of the numbered refs
options.site: on github.com but not on this page: a page, a person, a post, a section of it
options.web: elsewhere: another website, or a search of the whole web
